system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: A remote interactive logon as the sole IT administrator, omar.haddad, reached WS-BCARTER-01 from 192.0.2.45 at 13:40 UTC. The inventory says remote administration is only performed from WS-OHADDAD-01 and there is no VPN, so this access is inconsistent with the stated practice.

The domain controller recorded creation of it_helper by omar.haddad at 13:44 UTC, followed by addition of that account to the group named Administrators. This does not match the help-desk temporary-account practice, which uses tmp.<name> and grants no administrator rights.

During omar.haddad's session on WS-BCARTER-01, a scheduled task was registered to run PowerShell with a hidden window and an encoded command that decodes to an expression fetching and executing a script from http://192.0.2.45/a.ps1. This is strongly consistent with malicious payload delivery.

On WS-BCARTER-01, a Commvault GxCVD service process used explicit credentials for svc-claimsync to access FILE-HD-01. The inventory identifies ClaimSync and CobaltVault as separate approved services, places the ClaimSync job on FILE-HD-01, and identifies a different CobaltVault agent; this use is unexplained by the provided context.

known_telemetry_limitations: The scheduled-task registration is recorded, but the supplied evidence does not show whether the task ran or whether the script was successfully retrieved or executed.
The evidence does not identify who controlled 192.0.2.45 or establish whether that address was reachable at the time.
The supplied records do not show the subsequent use, modification, or removal of it_helper.
claims_not_established: Whether the it_helper account was used after creation.
Whether the scheduled task successfully executed its command or caused additional host changes.
Whether the svc-claimsync credential was compromised or used successfully against FILE-HD-01.
The identity of the operator behind the remote session and the source address.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect DC account and group-change audit details, including subsequent logons and changes for it_helper.
Collect task scheduler operational logs and process, PowerShell, and network telemetry from WS-BCARTER-01 for the task and script URL.
Investigate 192.0.2.45 using available firewall, proxy, routing, and remote-access records; verify whether it is an authorized source.
Review FILE-HD-01 authentication and service logs for svc-claimsync, and determine why the Commvault executable on WS-BCARTER-01 used that account.
Preserve and examine WS-BCARTER-01 and DC-HD-01 for related persistence, payloads, and account-management activity.
